findings.summary: CPU preflight subprocess cannot produce the artifact the launcher reads.
findings.failure_scenario: launch_once.py:162 runs cpu_preflight.py with --output. cpu_preflight.py (62 lines) defines run(output_dir) at line 23 and has no __main__ block and no argparse parser, although argparse is imported at line 5. The subprocess exits 0 and writes nothing. launch_once.py:168 then reads <output>/cpu-preflight-validation/cpu-preflight.json and raises FileNotFoundError. Even with an entrypoint, run() writes output_dir/cpu-preflight.json (cpu_preflight.py:61), not output_dir/cpu-preflight-validation/cpu-preflight.json. Result: every launch attempt fails before claim_once (launch_once.py:182), so no marker is consumed but the probe cannot run. README.md's documented preflight command is also a silent no-op. cpu-preflight-run.log was produced by an entrypoint that is not in the pinned source.

findings.summary: Zero MPS driver samples taken before the MPS model load fail a healthy run after the one-shot marker is claimed.
findings.failure_scenario: probe.py:197 starts the ResourceSampler before load_inference_model('best204', device='mps'). The sampler's _default_probe (worker.py, R6 frozen) reads torch.mps.driver_allocated_memory() every 0.25 s from sampler start. Startup samples taken before any MPS tensor exists can legitimately be 0. validate_representative_measurements (probe.py:117) requires all(value > 0), so the run is marked failed even when the workload is healthy. That happens after claim_once (launch_once.py:182), so the single authorized probe is consumed and a new review and reservation are required. Fix: require finite, nonnegative samples everywhere, and positive high-water only over samples after the MPS load timestamp. This needs a measured run to confirm; no hardware run was allowed here.

findings.summary: The 240-forward target may not be reachable inside the 45-second active bound at the measured per-pass rate.
findings.failure_scenario: Frozen evidence shows 16 forwards and 272 guards over 2 synthetic passes, so about 8 forwards and 136 guards per pass. The loop exits only when forwards >= 240 and elapsed >= 30 s. Reaching 240 forwards needs about 30 passes, about 1920 synthetic rows with per-row fsync (probe.py fsync sink), and about 4080 guards, all inside the 45 s active deadline. If per-pass time is above roughly 1.5 s, the guard raises at 45 s and the probe fails closed after claim_once. This is a risk to the acceptance target, not a logic error; the parent must measure it.

findings.summary: The 6 GiB cap is enforced in flight only for RSS; the MPS driver cap is checked only after the run.
findings.failure_scenario: The launcher monitor sums ps current RSS of launcher and worker and kills the group above 6 GiB. MPS driver allocation is never sampled by the launcher. probe.py checks mps_peak <= 6 GiB only after the workload finishes. A runaway MPS allocation therefore runs until the 45 s active or 90 s work deadline, not until the cap. Brief asks for separate 6 GiB RSS and MPS driver bounds; the MPS bound is post-hoc only.

findings.summary: Post-SIGKILL communicate() has no timeout, so the 120 s outer bound can be exceeded on a hung child.
findings.failure_scenario: On timeout the launcher sends SIGTERM, waits 5 s, then SIGKILL and calls process.communicate() with no timeout. If the child is stuck in an uninterruptible state, the launcher hangs past 120 s and the timeout evidence is never written.

findings.summary: Launcher leaves status child_reaped_postflight_pending if a later post-check fails.
findings.failure_scenario: launch_once.py:294 writes status child_reaped_postflight_pending before the post-child checks. If a later check raises, main()'s except (launch_once.py main) sees launcher-result.json already exists and does not overwrite it. A failed run therefore looks pending in evidence. Still fail-closed, but misleading.
